subject: Plotting inla bru predicted output covering the entire mesh

messages.author: 1dccea267c9abe1f
messages.subject: Plotting inla bru predicted output covering the entire mesh
parts:
Hello Inla discussion group,

I fitted a zap model to predict my bird probabilities and numbers using the link from the following example: https://inlabru-org.github.io/inlabru/articles/zip_zap_models.html. 

When I plot my predicted presence and number of birds, my predictions are shown as points on a mesh and do not cover the entire mesh. My predicted outputs are in the attached image. So my question is why my predictions are not covering the whole mesh. In the example given above, predictions cover the whole mesh. My connected second question would be, how could I have predictions covering my entire mesh, as in the example?

My code is given below.
I really appreciate the help.
Thank you in advance,
Morgane

bnd <- inla.nonconvex.hull(gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$geometry,convex=10*1000) # convex= -0.02)  #-0.03)  #convex=50*100) 

# Recommended settings:
RangeGuess <- 50 * 1000 #50
MaxEdge <- RangeGuess / 5

px_mesh <-fm_mesh_2d_inla(loc = gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$geometry,
                          max.edge = c(2500,5000)*MaxEdge, #c(2500,10000),
                          boundary = bnd,
                          cutoff = 1200,# is the smallest value between 2 sampling points
                          crs ="+proj=utm +zone=30 +datum=WGS84 +units=m"
                          )

plot(px_mesh)

px_matern <- INLA::inla.spde2.pcmatern(px_mesh,
  prior.range = c(50000, 0.01), #50*1000  
  prior.sigma = c(1.5, 0.01))

comps <- ~ horiz_speed_std(gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$horiz_speed_std) +
           Intercept_present(1) +
           Intercept_count(1) +
           dichla_std(gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$dichla_std[gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$present == TRUE]) 
         +   bottom_temp_std(gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$bottom_temp_std[gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$present == TRUE]) +
           field(geometry, model = px_matern)


#### best model so far
truncated_poisson_like_dichla <-
  if (package_version(getNamespaceVersion("INLA")) < "2023.10.19-1") {
    like(
      family = "zeroinflatedpoisson0",
      data = gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf[gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$present,],
      formula = count ~  bottom_temp_std+ dichla_std + field+ Intercept_count,
      E = area,
      control.family = list(hyper = list(theta = list(
        initial = -20, fixed = TRUE
      )))
    )
  } else {
    like(
      family = "nzpoisson",
      data = gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf[gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf$present,],
      formula = count ~ bottom_temp_std+ dichla_std+ field+ Intercept_count,
      E = area
    )
  }  

fit_zap_dichla <- bru(
  comps,
  like(
    family = "binomial",
    data = gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf,
    formula = binary ~ horiz_speed_std + Intercept_present
  ),
 
  truncated_poisson_like_dichla
)

summary(fit_zap_dichla)

# predict without windfarm
pred_zap_dichla <- predict(
  fit_zap_dichla,
  gannet_fvcom_nohigh_sf,
  ~ {
    presence_prob <-
    plogis(horiz_speed_std  + Intercept_present)
    lambda <- exp(bottom_temp_std+ dichla_std + field + Intercept_count)
    expect <- presence_prob * lambda * area / (1 - exp(-lambda * area))
    variance <- expect * (1 - exp(-lambda * area) * expect)
    list(
      presence = presence_prob,
      lambda = lambda,
      expect = expect,
      variance = variance,
      obs_prob = (1 - presence_prob) * (count == 0) +
        (count > 0) * presence_prob * dpois(count, expect) / (1 - dpois(0, expect))
    )
  },
  n.samples = 1000
)

presence_zap_dichla <- pred_zap_dichla$presence
expect_zap_dichla <- pred_zap_dichla$expect
expect_zap_dichla$pred_var <- pred_zap_dichla$variance$mean + expect_zap_dichla$sd^2
expect_zap_dichla$log_score <- -log(pred_zap_dichla$obs_prob$mean)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Plotting inla bru predicted output covering the entire mesh
parts:
You appear to have made predictions along the transects only. To
predict on the entire domain, you can likely just use fm_pixels() to
construct a grid of point on which to predict. See the distance
sampling examples on the inlabru github.io page for examples of such
prediction approaches.

Finn
